record.paper_title: Twenty Open Questions in Supersymmetric Particle Physics
record.original_question: N = 1 supersymmetric gauge theories exhibit proposed infrared dualities in which different gauge groups and matter descriptions flow to the same low-energy physics, such as SU(Nc) with Nf flavors being dual to SU(Nf − Nc) with Nf flavors in appropriate regimes. Can these duality conjectures be proved by an explicit map between degrees of freedom, what do they imply about whether gauge symmetry is fundamental or emergent in supersymmetric gauge theories, and to what extent do the duality relations survive supersymmetry breaking so that they can inform low-energy phenomenology?

evidence.quote: Question #16 N=1 SUSY duality: How has SUSY changed our view of gauge theory?
N = 1 dualities relate two seemingly different theories in the sense that both flow to the same fixed point in the infrared.
SU(Nc) with Nf flavors ⇔ SU(Nf − Nc) with Nf flavors as ‘dual’ theories.

The existence of such duality conjectures immediately prompts a number of outstanding questions. First, can one prove these conjectures?... Second, what does the existence of such dualities tell us about the fundamental nature of supersymmetric gauge theories?... Finally... to what extent do these duality relations survive supersymmetry breaking?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider four-dimensional N=1 supersymmetric gauge theories. The Seiberg duality conjecture asserts that, in the conformal window, an "electric" SU(N_c) gauge theory with N_f chiral superfields Q in the fundamental and N_f chiral superfields Q̃ in the antifundamental flows in the infrared to the same superconformal fixed point as a "magnetic" SU(N_f − N_c) gauge theory with N_f dual quarks q, q̃, a gauge-singlet meson superfield M^i_j transforming in the (fundamental, antifundamental) of the SU(N_f) × SU(N_f) flavor symmetry, and superpotential W = M^i_j q̃^j q_i. Address the following:

(a) Provide a rigorous proof of this infrared equivalence by exhibiting an explicit map between the gauge-invariant degrees of freedom (chiral ring operators, currents, and correlators) of the electric and magnetic theories, beyond the existing consistency checks ('t Hooft anomaly matching, superconformal index identities, moduli space matching, decoupling and deformation tests).

(b) Determine what the existence of such infrared dualities, in which two distinct ultraviolet gauge groups produce the same low-energy physics, implies about whether the gauge symmetry of an N=1 supersymmetric gauge theory is a fundamental property of the theory or merely an emergent, redundant description of its infrared dynamics.

(c) Determine to what extent these duality relations are preserved when supersymmetry is broken (either softly or spontaneously); in particular, identify which dual observables (spectra, condensates, effective potentials, phase structure) continue to match after SUSY breaking, and quantify how such surviving duality relations can be used to extract information about the low-energy phenomenology of non-supersymmetric gauge theories.
artifact.status_search_result: Seiberg duality between SU(N_c) and SU(N_f − N_c) with N_f flavors remains a conjecture supported by extensive evidence (‘t Hooft anomaly matching, superconformal index identities, brane constructions, moduli space and deformation checks) but lacks a rigorous field-theoretic proof. Questions about gauge symmetry being emergent and the fate of duality under SUSY breaking are still active research topics.

status_evidence.title: Seiberg duality - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Seiberg duality remains a conjecture; evidence includes 't Hooft anomaly matching and superconformal index identities, but a rigorous field-theoretic proof has not been given.
status_evidence.claim: Seiberg duality is still a conjecture, supported by strong but indirect evidence.

status_evidence.title: Seiberg duality in nLab
status_evidence.snippet: Seiberg duality is realized via D-brane constructions and many consistency checks but is not derived from first principles.
status_evidence.claim: No first-principles proof of Seiberg duality exists.

status_evidence.title: Confinement in N=1 SQCD: One Step Beyond Seiberg's Duality
status_evidence.snippet: Continued research extending Seiberg duality and its phenomenological consequences under deformations, including SUSY-breaking perturbations.
status_evidence.claim: Extensions to SUSY-breaking deformations remain an active subject.
